intro: Step down into Binbirdirek Cistern, in İstanbul province, from the 4th century AD. It is the city's second largest covered cistern. Look at its 224 columns: each is two shafts set one on the other, and you can still see the stone collars at the joins.
history: The cistern was built in the fourth century beneath the palace of the consul Philoxenos, and it is the city's second largest covered cistern after the Basilica Cistern. Under the Ottomans it was drained and served as a spinning workshop. Its name means 'a thousand and one columns' — there are in fact 224.
highlights: As you wander among the 224 columns, don't miss the two-part column shafts and the stone collars that join them — and look up at the brick vaults.
facts: Did you know? Single shafts were not tall enough, so the columns are built in two pieces, and the stone collars at the joins declare the join rather than hide it. And the name 'a thousand and one columns' is a generous one: there are in fact 224.
outro: This brings our journey through Binbirdirek Cistern to an end. Before you go, a small request: please leave the stones untouched, keep to the marked paths and carry water with you. These columns have stood for centuries; let them keep standing for those who come after you. Enjoy your visit.
